text: The Magician Cloak is a mid game light armor piece in Final Fantasy IX for magic users. It teaches Insomniac, which immunizes against Sleep, and MP+10%. The Magician Cloak strengthens the wearer's Ice damage and is used for synthesis. Wearing it boosts the character's Magic stat when they level up. Like many equipment pieces in Final Fantasy IX, the Magician Cloak is named after the Wizard Clothing from Final Fantasy Tactics.

Magician's Bracelet is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has poor stats but four single materia slots. It provides +7 to and . Four is the most slots any armor has, so unless the player has a better four-slot armor, they can make do with the magician's bracelet until they get a better one if they want to maximize the number of materia the wearer equips.

Major Odilon is an enemy in Final Fantasy Type-0. He is a ranking officer in the Militesi Empire who pilots a Colossus-type magitek armor and is encountered in Mission 3-1, "The Infiltration of Iscah". In addition to piloting a Colossus, Major Odilon shares his in-game model, moveset, and Rubicus entry with it.

The Magus Hat is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a weak hat that Zidane, Vivi, Dagger, Quina, Eiko, Cinna, Marcus, and Blank can wear, though Blank and Cinna are not in the party when the Magus Hat is available in a normal playthrough. It teaches the Black Magic spell Slow to Vivi, which slows down a target so they get fewer turns in battle. The Magus Hat is used for synthesis and boosts the wearer's Ice damage, making it excellent for Vivi.

Mako Cannon Rampage is the thirty-fourth chapter of Final Fantasy VII, and the fourth chapter of the fourth act, "Decisive Battle". After Cloud Strife's party left the City of the Ancients, the Diamond Weapon attacked Midgar, following which Cait Sith reported Professor Hojo using the Sister Ray to charge toward Northern Cave. The party fought Diamond Weapon, before commencing a raid on Midgar to stop Hojo and defeat the Shinra Electric Power Company. This chapter can be skipped with the Raid on Midgar glitch.

The Mantra Band is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a mid tier headband that everyone but Steiner and Freya can wear. It teaches the passive abilities Antibody, which inoculates against Poison, and HP+20%. The headband provides minor level up bonuses to Magic and Spirit, both generally good stats to boost, especially for mages.

Manuscripts are items in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission" used to provide skill points for purchasing weapon upgrades, as well as second level limit breaks. Manuscripts are gained for completing various objectives, including Corneo Colosseum and Shinra Combat Simulator challenges, and by defeating certain enemies in hard mode. Manuscripts are necessary to fully level up weapons after a character reaches their maximum level 50. There are 56 manuscripts in total in the base game. During an initial playthrough, only 12 can be obtained, and the remaining 44 require hard mode difficulty. There are 14 per character. The mechanic returns in INTERmission for Yuffie and Sonon. Manuscripts differ for each character. Cloud's are known as The Art of Swordplay, Barret's are known as Sharpshooter's Companion, Tifa's are the Way of the Fist, and Aerith's are Telluric Scriptures. Limit breaks being learned from books alludes to the original Final Fantasy VII where each party member's final Limit was learned from a manual, which often required doing a sidequest to find.

The Martial Tank is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It launches Support Machine+s, which should be taken out first. Martial Tank is powerful, but slow, so it is easy to dodge its attacks and keep behind it. Tri-Thundaga is the best method of attack against it, but if that's not available, using any Lightning-elemental attacks or Punch-type attacks will work. When the Martial Tank gets low enough on HP, it'll use Eject! to summon five Support Machine+ enemies.

The Marshalist's Staff is Sonon's default weapon in "Episode INTERmission" in Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. It teaches the Swirling Storm ability, a powerful, multi-hitting attack. It is learned faster by finishing off the enemy with the ability. The Marshalist's Staff favors over , but both grow evenly through upgrades. Its unlocked abilities significantly increase Sonon's Max HP, and unlock the ability to synergize Yuffie and Sonon's limit breaks, but otherwise don't focus on any specific field.

The Master Blade is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It is similar in appearance to that of the Moth Slasher. Zack should be equipped with the Super Ribbon. The Master Blade's deadly Drill Attack will reduce Zack's HP to 1 if it connects. The best way to defeat it is to use hit-and-run tactic: hit it with Costly Punch, dodge its attack, then keep moving.
The Master Dogi is a piece of armor exclusive to the 3D versions of Final Fantasy III. It provides 54 Defense, 23 Magic Defense, +10 Mind, and +10 Agility. It can be used by the Black Belt class.
The Mega Armor is an enemy in Final Fantasy VI. The Mega Armor does not appear on the Veldt, and it does not have a Rage either.

The Mech Dragon, also known as the Clockwork Dragon, Mech D., or D.Machin, is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV. It is a particularly evasive and rare monster when attempting to complete the bestiary in the GBA and subsequent versions. It only appears on the floor before the final floor and on the Giant of Babil's Inner Stair (the same place where the Elemental Lords are fought). The long, bridge-like area it appears in and its low encounter rate is a reference to Warmech from Final Fantasy. Besides the Inner Stair, a Siren can also be used to summon one in certain other areas of the dungeon. It is also one of the monsters that the enemy Searcher can summon.

The Mech Soldier, also known as the Machine or Clockwork Soldier, is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV. The Mech Soldier is a mechanical enemy that is weak to Lightning. It is one of the weakest enemies within the Giant. When struck with a Lightning-elemental attack, it will ignore the party and battle its comrade for a time. This makes it easy to decimate even large groups of them.

Mech Guard is a machina enemy in Final Fantasy X encountered in the desert of Bikanel. It is not dangerous, with relatively low Strength and low Agility. As with all machina enemies, using the Steal command will instantly defeat it. If Provoked, it will use a less accurate physical attack, and will not attack whatsoever against Valefor. Mech Guard drops armor with any of the SOS elemental defenses. It also drops weapons with any of the elemental strikes.

Mech Leader is a machina enemy in Final Fantasy X encountered on Mt. Gagazet. It uses both a standard attack and Electrocute that will cause Lightning-elemental damage. It will just use Electrocute against aeons, or nothing against Valefor. When Provoked, it uses an attack with reduced accuracy. As with most machina enemies, using the steal command on it will instantly defeat it. Mech Leader drops armor with any of the SOS elemental defenses. It also drops weapons with any of the elemental strikes.

Mech Gunner is a machina enemy in Final Fantasy X encountered in the desert of Bikanel. As with all machina enemies, using Steal on it will instantly defeat it. If Provoked, it will use a less accurate physical attack, and will not attack whatsoever against the aeon Valefor. Mech Gunners drop armor with any of the SOS elemental defenses as well as SOS Protect, SOS Shell, or SOS Reflect. It also drops weapons with any of the elemental strikes.

Mech Defender is a machina enemy in Final Fantasy X encountered on Mt. Gagazet. It will use a physical attack with reduced accuracy if Provoked, and will not attack Valefor. As with most machina enemies, using the Steal command on it will instantly defeat it. Mech Defender drops armor with any of the SOS elemental defenses as well as SOS Protect, SOS Shell, or SOS Reflect. It will also drop weapons with any of the elemental strikes.

Mech is a category of enemies in Final Fantasy X and Final Fantasy X-2. Mechs are a form of machine, or 'machina', but have notable differences compared to enemies classified as machina. In Final Fantasy X, mechs cannot be instantly destroyed by Steal, while machina can. Mechs have a stone-like appearance while most machina appear to be metallic, and some mechs are used by Yevon. All mechs use status attacks and multiple chain attacks.

Mech Hunter is a machina enemy in Final Fantasy X fought in the Cavern of the Stolen Fayth alongside the fiends Imp and Epaaj. As a machina, it is weak against lightning-elemental attacks and can have Al Bhed Potions bribed or stolen from it. As with most machina, stealing from it instantly kills it. It will use a physical attack with reduced accuracy when Provoked, and will not attack the aeon Valefor.
Max Ray , also known as Supernal Ray, is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.

The Metal Jerkin is a mid-ranked light armor in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's defense by 31 (Zodiac) or 26 (original), and HP by 280. Despite having "metal" in the name, Metal Jerkin does not count as metallic equipment for the Magnetize debuff in the Vinuskar boss battle.

The Mesmeric Armlet is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It prioritizes magical defense over physical defense, and has two unlinked materia slots. Its complement piece is the Leather Bracer. The Mesmeric Armlet provides +26 to and +6 to . It is good to replace the early equipment purchasable from Sector 7 slums.
Mid-sized Carrier is an enemy in Final Fantasy Type-0. A warship used by the Militesi Empire, it drops soldiers on the battlefield.

Midgar Bangle is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has one materia slot and provides +18 to and . It is good to equip to replace the Bronze Bangles Cloud and Tifa start with, and is slightly better than the iron bangle.

The Minerva's Plate is an endgame light armor piece in Final Fantasy IX for female characters. It teaches High Tide, which allows the character enter Trance more frequently, and Restore HP, which restores HP to the character when they survive an attack in Near Death. The plate gives a bonus to the wearer's Strength and Magic when they level up with it equipped and is needed for synthesis.
Moogle Rod is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series. It is a rod fashioned after the series's mascot creature, moogle.
(SR).]] Moonlight Wand is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.

Mr. Clio is a non-playable character in Final Fantasy V, located in the Unknown Cave. To reach the cave, a submarine is needed, submerging it south of Karnak. When spoken to, he will tell the player various statistics such as the number of treasures found and number of enemies slain. Prior to the Game Boy Advance version, the character went unnamed.
Mt. Badu is a daily quest in King's Knight -Wrath of the Dark Dragon-, available every Monday. This quest offers increased drops of Fire Orbs, used in weapon and skill synthesis.

The Mythril Mail, also styled as the Mithril Mail, is a low-ranked suit of heavy armor in Final Fantasy VI. It can be equipped by Terra, Locke, Edgar, Cyan, Celes, and Setzer to provide 51 defense and 34 magic defense. Betting the Mythril Mail in the Dragon's Neck Coliseum will pit the player against Typhon.

The Mythril Bracers is an arm armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 2 Defense, 3 Magic Defense, and 7% Evasion in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions, it provides 2 Defense, 4 Magic Defense, +1 Intellect, and +1 Mind. It can be used by the Onion Knight, White Mage, Black Mage, Red Mage, Scholar, Geomancer, Evoker, Bard, Devout, Magus, Summoner, and Sage classes in all versions, while in the 3D versions, it can be used by the Freelancer class.

Naglfar is a superboss in Final Fantasy XV fought during the Wondrous Weapon sidequest for Randolph in Chapter 15. Completing the quest yields the superb Zwill Crossblades daggers. The Squirming Bone key item naglfar yields is the only "monster part" obtained from a daemon. Usually only biological monsters drop monster parts, whereas daemons dissolve into miasma upon being defeated. The description to Squirming Bone describes it as "the partial remains of a deathclaw, still wriggling with life."

Negalmuur is a Rare Game in Final Fantasy XII appearing in the Ward of the Sword-King area of the Stilshrine of Miriam. It is a weaker form of the Nightwalker and widely used as a way to auto-level, because it frequently summons undead enemies.

Necrotic Entity is an enemy in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, encountered in the Shinra-8 cruise ship during Chapter 5, fought with Cloud and Tifa. The creature is later fought in Costa del Sol prior to the battle against the Grasptropod in Chapter 6. It is also fought in the Shinra Manor's Chadley Combat Simulator in the Nibel Region. They are black-robed men which have been assimilated by the Experimental Varghidpolis, creatures infused with Jenova's cells created by Shinra's R&D Division. Professor Hojo later captures some of these abominations to acquire their DNA samples in order to further fuel his research.

Nether Blade, also known as Dia Sword Back, is a Nether Mantra ability in Final Fantasy Tactics, available for the netherseer job. It charges a spell that deals massive wind-elemental damage to units within the effect radius, capable of striking multiple times per tile. The action ability must be learned by expending JP earned for the netherseer job. The only playable netherseer is Marach Galthena. Other abilities that deal wind damage include the geomancer's Wind Slash & Wind Blast, and the skyseer's Adamantine Blade, which is also Nether Blade's counterpart.
The nightblade, originally localized as knight blade, is an enemy job in Final Fantasy Tactics. It is exclusive to Isilud and combines the attributes of the knight and the dragoon.

Ninja Suit is a light armor piece in Final Fantasy V. Despite its name, it is not just for the Ninja: it is able to be equipped by Knight, Monk, Thief, Dragoon, Ninja, Samurai, Berserker, Ranger, Mystic Knight, Blue Mage, Red Mage, Beastmaster, Chemist, Dancer, Cannoneer, Gladiator, Mime, and Freelancer classes.

Ninja Armlet is a piece of armor in "Episode INTERmission" in Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. It has one set of linked materia slots and one single slot, and provides +38 to and . It is a good armor piece with balanced defense, which also doubles the amount of AP earned for all materia slotted into it; though this was a trait to some armor pieces in the original Final Fantasy VII, none such armor were used in the base Final Fantasy VII Remake.
Nomad is an enemy in Final Fantasy Type-0 appearing in the third mission. It is a weapon used by the Militesi Empire to scout intruders.

Oblitzerator is a boss in Final Fantasy X. It is a machina weapon commanded by the Al Bhed and is fought by Tidus, Lulu, and Kimahri on a ship leaving from Luca Dock No. 4 after the Al Bhed Psyches kidnap Yuna. It fights by shooting blitzballs at the party.
.]] Nutkin Suit is a recurring armor piece in the Final Fantasy series that makes the wearer look like a nutkin.
Nymurod is an enemy in Final Fantasy Type-0 encountered in the fourth and sixth chapters. It is a tripedal tank-like weapon.
Ogopogo is a boss from Final Fantasy IV fought in Lunar Subterrane. It guards Edge's most powerful weapon, the Masamune.

The Omega Slave is a field boss duo in Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers, and are the strongest variation of the Crystal Armor foes. They can be found in the remains of the Aerial Prison.
One For All is an ability learned by the Rune Fencer (level 95) in Final Fantasy XI. It grants Magic Shield for party members within the area of effect.

The Onion Gauntlets is an arm armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 32 Defense, 32 Magic Defense, 32% Evasion, +5 Strength, +5 Vitality, and +5 Agility in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions, it provides 50 Defense, 25 Magic Defense, +3 to all stats, and immunity to all statuses . It can be used by the Onion Knight class.
The Optic Blaster is an enemy in Final Fantasy IV: The After Years exclusive to Final Fantasy IV: The Complete Collection. It can be summoned by the Giant's Chest as part of the superboss Lost Babil.

Owe is a playable character of War of the Visions: Final Fantasy Brave Exvius. Known as the Seeker of Blade Souls, he is a member of the Knights of Leonis within the Fortem division. He is Sterne's sword instructor.

The Paladin's Shield, also known as the Paladin Shld, is the strongest shield in Final Fantasy VI. The shield provides great stats, but moreover, absorbs or nullifies most elements. It also teaches the Ultima spell. Though the shield is extremely strong, it is also very difficult to acquire, as one must first use the Cursed Shield.
Paramina Crossbow is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.
Panjandrum is an enemy in Final Fantasy Type-0. It is a weapon used by the Militesi Empire which detects intruders. It appears only in the missions in Chapter 3.
The Phantom Forest is a location in Final Fantasy VI and is where the Phantom Train departs. The forest contains a recovery spring, and there is a path that loops back to the entrance.

The Phorusracos is an enemy from Final Fantasy II. It appears as a random encounter around the area where the Palamecian army keeps its Dreadnought after launching it from Bafsk; and northwest of Fynn. It can be eliminated easily with physical attacks and offensive spells. The enemy only appears on the world map, and once the Cyclone appears and the formations change, the Phorusracos can no longer be fought, making it a missable enemy for the Bestiary unless the player transverses through the Arcane Labyrinth, which is available only in the 20th Anniversary Edition, iOS, and Android versions.
Pile Banger , also known as Pilebunkers, is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series.
Platinum Fist is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series. It is part of the platinum equipment set.
.]] Platinum Deck is a recurring card deck weapon in the Final Fantasy series associated with Ace of Class Zero. It is part of platinum equipment.

The Platina Armor is a late game heavy body armor in Final Fantasy IX for Steiner and Freya. It teaches Beast Killer, which improves damage to beast type enemies. It halves Ice damage to the wearer. Like many equipment pieces in Final Fantasy IX, the Platina Armor is based on an equipment piece from Final Fantasy Tactics.
The Pluto Armor, formerly called PlutoArmor and PlutArmr, is an enemy in Final Fantasy VI fought in the Dreamscape.

as Lady Luck in Final Fantasy X-2 holding playing cards.]] :For the weapon in Final Fantasy Type-0, see: Playing Cards (Type-0) Playing cards are pieces paper or similar thin material marked with distinguishing motifs used for playing card games. The deck of 52 is the most common deck of playing cards used in the real world, and elements of it are also common in the Final Fantasy series. The standard 52-card deck includes thirteen ranks of each of the four French suits: clubs (♣), diamonds (♦), hearts (♥) and spades (♠). Each suit includes an ace, a king, queen and jack, and ranks two through ten. Anywhere from one to six (most often two or three) jokers are added to commercial decks, as some card games require extra cards. Besides playing card games, the cards are also sometimes used for fortune-telling. This is known as . In English-speaking countries the most common form of cartomancy is . Tarot Cards is a recurring accessory in the series that boosts one's proficiency in magic in some way. Final Fantasy games also have dedicated card games that appear as minigames and collectibles in the game's world. Final Fantasy trading card games have also been released by Square Enix, the Final Fantasy Trading Card Game being the most notable. Cards have also appeared as weapons associated with the Gambler class. This article is for the phenomenon. For the weapon type, see Card (weapon type). For a list of card games, both real world and minigame, see Card games.

Poles , also called stick, are a recurring weapon type from the Final Fantasy series, shown mostly in the Ivalice Alliance. It is not wielded by the same job in two games, but it is often used by light melee and mage jobs. Most poles are recurring, and the Whale Whisker is usually the strongest of the type.
Poncho , also known as Windbreaker, is a recurring armor piece in the Final Fantasy series.

The Power Sash is light armor in Final Fantasy VI. It can be equipped by Locke, Sabin, Shadow, Cyan, and Gau to provides 52 defense and 35 magic defense, as well as +1 speed and +5 to stamina and strength. Betting the Power Sash in the Dragon's Neck Coliseum will pit the player against Typhon. It is good for a physical fighter for its +5 to strength, such as Edgar.

The Power Bracers is an arm armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 4 Defense, 1 Magic Defense, 11% Evasion, and +5 Strength in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions, it provides 13 Defense, 9 Magic Defense, +2 Strength, and +2 Vitality. It can be used by the Onion Knight, Warrior, Monk, Ranger, Knight, Thief, Dragoon, Viking, Black Belt, and Ninja classes in all versions, while in the 3D versions, it can be used by the Freelancer class.

The power garb, also known as the Power Sleeve in the PlayStation version, is a good light body armor piece in Final Fantasy Tactics, equipped by all job classes except for knights (including most special knights), dragoons, samurai, mimes, and the dragonkin. Unusually for a body armor piece, it raises the wearer's physical strength.

The power gauntlet, also known as the Power Wrist in the PlayStation version, is an armguard in Final Fantasy Tactics worn in the accessory slot by any human unit. It raises the wearer's physical prowess.

The Prima Vista is the airship that Ramza bas Lexentale, his sister Alma bas Lexentale, and their father Jenomis cen Lexentale used to travel the Garlean Empire to perform their stage plays. Later, his family was exiled from the Empire so they traveled to Kugane via this same airship.

Reaper Clan Warmachine is a mission boss from Final Fantasy XI: Rise of the Zilart. It is encountered in San d'Oria Mission 7-2: The Secret Weapon, alongside Darokbok of Clan Reaper, Derakbak of Clan Wolf, Jagidbod of Clan Reaper, and the Wolf Clan Warmachine.
.]] Death's Scythe , also known as Reaper's Scythe, is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series. It is a scythe that has come to be associated as the weapon of Sice from Class Zero.
Red Saucer I is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. Red Saucer I poses little threat and is quickly dispatched with a few sword swings.

The Red Saucer II is an enemy from Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It poses little threat and a few standard sword attacks will bring it down. It is best to eliminate the Saucer quickly to prevent it from casting Barrier for its cohorts.

Rune Fencer is one of the jobs released in the Final Fantasy XI: Seekers of Adoulin expansion. Rune Fencer is the third "tank"-type job, and the first job to specialize in the use of the greatsword. Rune Fencers are intended to use their damage-dealing capabilities to help draw the foe's attention and use their spells and special job abilities to mitigate magic damage. Rune Fencer's magical attacks and defenses have a strong elemental aspect, determined by which runes they are "harboring" at the time. Built-up harbored runes provide elemental attack and defense, and furthermore can be expended for various effects.

The Rune Bracers is an arm armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 5 Defense, 6 Magic Defense, and 10% Evasion in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions, it provides 11 Defense, 13 Magic Defense, +2 Intellect, +2 Mind, and immunity to Petrify, Toad, and Mini. It can be used by the Onion Knight, White Mage, Black Mage, Red Mage, Scholar, Geomancer, Evoker, Bard, Devout, Magus, Summoner, and Sage classes in all versions, while in the 3D versions, it can be used by the Freelancer class.

SOLDIER: 1st is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII. They carry a piece of armor called Shinra Alpha, which is quite strong and worth stealing, as it cannot be bought in any store. Offensively, the SOLDIER uses many powerful physical attacks. They can use Fight twice in one turn, while Sword of Doom is only used when his HP drops below 25%. They also use Silence as a counter to magical attacks. He uses Quadra-Cut when his HP drops below 75%. SOLDIER: 1sts are not immune to any status except Manipulate, making Bad Breath and Hades good against them, and they are susceptible to L4 Suicide.

The Rusty Mail is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy III. It provides 0 Defense and 1 Magic Defense in the 2D versions, while in the 3D versions it provides 0 Defense and 0 Magic Defense. It can be used by the Onion Knight, Warrior, Knight, Dragoon, Viking, Dark Knight, and Ninja classes in all versions, and the Freelancer class in the 3D versions. Despite it being listed for classes in the 2D versions, it cannot be equipped at all in the 2D versions.

Square Enix - Airship Cruise Beats is a digital only, electronic dance music arrange album, featuring tracks from various Square Enix video games, including the Final Fantasy series. A video of the album as well as other dance tracks from other Square Enix Music albums, including was officially uploaded to Square Enix Music's YouTube page as part of the launch of the channel.

The Steepled Hat is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX. It is a weak hat that Zidane, Vivi, Dagger, Quina, Eiko, Cinna, Marcus, and Blank can wear, though Blank and Cinna are not in the party when the Steepled Hat is available in a normal playthrough. It boosts the wearer's Strength on level up. The Steepled Hat teaches the White Magic spell Protect to Dagger and Eiko, which halves physical damage taken to one target. The Steepled Hat is used for synthesis and is notable for being an ingredient for the gil farming "Cotton Robe trick".

Steal Weapon is a Steal action ability in Final Fantasy Tactics, learned by the thief job. It attempts to steal an adjacent enemy's equipped weapon, adding it to the player's inventory. It has no charge time and costs no MP. The action ability must be learned by expending JP earned for the thief job. In The War of the Lions version, the sky pirate has access to the Plunder Weapon ability, which has around 10% increased success rate compared to Steal Weapon.

The Steel Pincers are a melee weapon for Barret in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It provides the Charging Uppercut ability, a melee ability that allows Barret to deal tremendous single target damage. The Steel Pincers are one of two melee weapons for Barret along with the . Between the two, Steel Pincers give Barret a higher attribute, but a slightly lower attribute (although still the second-highest of any of his weapons). Between Barret's melee weapons, Steel Pincers is therefore best if players do not wish to sacrifice his magic ability too heavily.

The Steel Mask is a mid to high ranked heavy armor helm in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 32 (Zodiac) or 28 (original), Strength by 7 and Speed by 4. The latter makes it potentially good for those who wield weapons that take the Speed stat into account for damage calculation: bows, daggers and ninja swords. However, in the Zodiac versions, the heavy armor jobs don't unlock these weapon types. The Steel Mask is metallic for the purposes of the Magnetize debuff present in the boss battles against Vinuskar and Ultima, and is the "heaviest" with the largest penalty to speed in these battles among all the helms.

The Steel Reaper is a weapon for Yuffie Kisaragi in "Episode INTERmission" in Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. It teaches the Banishment ability, a powerful attack that deals more damage the more ATB gauges Yuffie has used in battle before casting it and takes on the active element from Elemental Ninjutsu. The steel reaper provides a higher bonus than its bonus, however its magic attack is not significantly lower than Yuffie's other weapons. Many of its unlocked abilities further improve Yuffie's physical attacks.

.]] Stoneblade , also known as Gorgon Blade, Medusa Sword, Basilisk Steel, or Break Blade, is a recurring weapon in the Final Fantasy series. The weapon commonly inflicts petrify status or is earth-elemental, and is usually a mid to high-rank weapon.

The following is a list of armor in Stranger of Paradise Final Fantasy Origin. Armor is usually obtained as rewards from quests, looted from various locations, purchased from the Dragon King Exchange Shop, and are dropped by defeated enemies and bosses. Each armor set is made up of four to five pieces, each with its own trio of special effects. As of Patch 1.21, The Rift Labyrinth adds new reskins of the Lufenian armor.

The Street Fighter series is a fighting game series developed and published by Capcom, which features a guest character from the Final Fantasy series. The series focuses on the affairs and happenings behind the individual participants of the premier hand-to-hand martial arts global event known as the World Warrior tournaments, and their reasons and motivations for participating to be recognized as the greatest martial artists and fighters in the world. The series is known for evolving and popularizing the foundational aspects of the current day fighting game genre.
Submarine Crew is an enemy from Final Fantasy VII. The party will not pose after defeating the two Submarine Crew enemies before boarding the submarine.

The Submarine Game ("Torpedo Attack" on the machine) is a replay of the battle for the Huge Materia near the Underwater Reactor in Final Fantasy VII. It becomes available on Part 2 after it has been played in the storyline. The game is located on the second floor of the Wonder Square at Gold Saucer and costs 200 gil to play.

Studded Bracer is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It has good stats and two linked materia slots. It provides +40 to and +10 to . It is the best physical defense armor at the time it first becomes available.

Named as such because the world of Final Fantasy VII does not feature traditional jobs, Styles determine what melee weapon a SOLDIER candidate wields, as well as which Trait, Ability and Skill they have available for them. † introduced in Season 2 ‡ introduced in Season 3 ◊ introduced in Season 4
Sumbha is an enemy in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. Although it has high Attack and Magic ratings, Sumbha is easy to defeat with sword attacks or magic spells. It absorbs fire.
Support Machine is a boss in Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. It is fought together with General's Tank.

Supreme Bracer is a piece of armor in Final Fantasy VII Remake and "Episode INTERmission". It has good stats, prioritizing physical defense, providing +62 to and +16 to . It has three materia slots, two of them linked. It is a an excellent piece of armor for physical defense, only second to the iron maiden that has no materia slots.
Superstar Belt is an accessory in Final Fantasy VII Remake that has the wearer essentially gain the Reprieve weapon passive ability on an accessory; the user avoids incapacitation once per battle.
Sword Rat, also known as SwordRat, is a enemy from Final Fantasy IV. In battle it counters all physical attacks with its powerful Needle attack, which causes a lot of damage.

The swordless Runic bug is a bug in Final Fantasy VI that involves the Runic battle command. Runic and Bushido require a sword or equivalent weapon to make them available for use in battle. Bushido works properly; if the character is improperly equipped, Bushido will not be available. Runic on the other hand is faulty, in that if a character is acting automatically (Dragon's Neck Coliseum, Confuse, Charm), that character can use Runic regardless of what weapon is currently equipped. The Runic command is enabled by the following weapons: all daggers, all spears, all katanas, and the Magus Rod. ru:Ошибка Рун без меча
Swordsman is an enemy in Final Fantasy Dimensions. It can be fought on the Warship.
Sword Oath is a spell from Final Fantasy XIV. It was removed in Final Fantasy XIV: Shadowbringers.

Sylph gloves are a weapon for Tifa's in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. The weapon includes the Reverse Gale ability, a -based physical attack. Though still providing strong physical damage, the sylph gloves have stats and weapon skills more weighted toward magic damage than most of her other weapons.

The Fierce is a boss fought in the Citadel as part of the final boss gauntlet in the Windows and Royal Editions of Final Fantasy XV. The Weapon's Refrain, commonly abbreviated by players as UWU (for "Ultima Weapon (Ultimate)") is an released in Patch 4.31, "Under the Moonlight", of Final Fantasy XIV: Stormblood. Unlocking the raid requires completion of , then speaking to the Wandering Minstrel in Kugane. Like before it, Free Trial players are barred from participating. The duty comprises of a single encounter, where players fight the game's original three primals—Garuda, Ifrit, and Titan—in succession, before once again facing off against Lahabrea and then the Ultima Weapon as it repeatedly summons the three primals. The primal encounters have a twist on their previous incarnations that plays off player expectations from having faced each of them three times before (in their Normal, Hard, and Extreme s), as the party must "improperly" act on some of their mechanics to trigger an empowered "Awoken" form to survive the phase transition into the Ultima Weapon. The mechanic is not immediately apparent as each primal can be defeated without awakening them, but this inevitably results in the party's death.

The Thief Hat is a light armor headgear in Final Fantasy IX for Zidane. It teaches Long Reach, which has Zidane do full damage from the back row; Lucky Seven, which deals fixed damage but Zidane's HP needs to end in a 7; and Mug, which makes Steal do minor damage. It grants a +2 level up bonus to Speed.

The Thief's Cap is a mid to high-ranked light armor headgear in Final Fantasy XII that boosts the wearer's magickal defense by 40 (Zodiac) or 36 (original), HP by 460, and Speed by +4. It can thus be a good headgear for those who use weapons that take the wielder's Speed stat into account: bows and daggers and ninja swords. However, a helm that boosts Strength has a bigger impact on the damage dealt.
The Thief's Gloves is an armor in Final Fantasy II. It provides 15 defense, -3% evasion, 5% Magic Defense, and -40 Intelligence/Spirit.

The Thief's Armlet is an armor piece in the Final Fantasy I & II: Dawn of Souls and the Final Fantasy 20th Anniversary PlayStation Portable and the now-discontinued iOS and iPadOS and Windows Phone versions of Final Fantasy (but not in the also now-discontinued Android version). It can be used by Thief and Ninja and provides 30 defense and 1 weight, as well as +5 to the wearer's agility.
The Tin Armor is Steiner's ultimate body armor in Final Fantasy IX. It has the best defensive stats but no abilities, elemental properties, or level up stat boosts.
Titan Bangle is an armor in Final Fantasy VII. It is a low ranked armor piece available fairly early on.

The Toughskin in Final Fantasy Tactics Advance is a green turtle-like creature with a sword sticking out of its back. It has an extremely high Defense stat, so magic spells are much more effective compared to physical attacks. Its Resonance ability can also disable the weapons used by most physically orientated jobs, further necessitating the use of magic. Toughskins can be dangerous against physical units with low MP, as it can use Matra Magic to invert the HP and MP of a target. To avoid this attack, it is best to keep a distance by using long-range bows and magic. Matra Magic can also be learned by the Blue Mage job as a Blue Magic ability. The Toughskin has an even hardier lavender cousin, the Blade Biter.

Town of Hero is a location in The Final Fantasy Legend, located southeast of Base Town. The Castle of Shield is near the town while the Castle of Armor is to the northeast, and the Castle of Sword is in the southeast mountains.

The train graveyard is a location in the Final Fantasy VII series. It is an abandoned switchyard in the Sector 7 slums of Midgar. Originally used as a switchyard for trains to transport between the undercity and onto the plate, the area became a junkyard of old and abandoned trains, creating a maze of rusted metal; an example of the Shinra Electric Power Company's neglect. Strong winds make the dilapidated carriages creak and groan, and odd high-pitched sounds echo over the area. The area is a dangerous lurking ground for monsters, especially of the supernatural variety.
The Traitor's Bow is a bow in Final Fantasy XII. In the original version, its license costs 45 LP. In the Zodiac versions, its license costs 70 LP and it can be used by the Archer.

Tristan is a Lilty ferryman who mans the ship which crosses the Jegon River from Ironmine Downs to Plains of Fum and back in Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles. Later in the game he will also use Port Tipa as a destination and carry the Caravanners across the ocean to Mount Kilanda or to the city of Leuda and the Lynari Desert beyond it. Tristan offers trips across the river for 50 gil per person or 100 gil between the Tipa Peninsula and Ironmine Downs or Plains of Fum. It is 500 gil for a player to sail out to sea. Tristan will give characters a discount if they provide him some Kilanda Sulfur from the volcano. He increases the discount if you provide him with a cactus flower from Lynari Desert. After both discounts, he also sells a pass for 50,000 gil to ride the boat free of charge from then on. He also apparently was a soldier in the city, as one of the Lilties close to ferry boat explains.

Trial of the Magians is a system in Final Fantasy XI primarily for obtaining, augmenting and upgrading weapons and armor to a higher level. The system is also used to unlock the job-specific Emotes. In order to undertake a trial, the player must hand over the equipment to be augmented or upgraded to the appropriate moogle, who will inscribe the trial information on the equipment, hand it back, and tell the player the task that must be completed a set number of times to complete the trial. Example tasks include killing a specific Notorious Monster, killing monsters of a certain family (optionally with a specific method, or under a certain Weather), using a certain weapon skill a certain number of times, or turning in a specific number of a certain item to the Delivery Crate at the side of one of the Magian moogles who supervises the trials. When the trial is completed, the equipment must be handed over to the moogle again, who will work special Moogle magic on it and hand it back. The most important use of the Trial of the Magians is to upgrade relic weapons, Mythic Weapons, and Empyrean Weapons from level 75 to level 99. However, by opening the Splintery Chest at the side of the lead moogle, players may obtain free weapons that may be upgraded and specialized using the trial system.
Tros is a Cephalopod fiend in Final Fantasy X that appears when Tidus and the then unnamed Rikku try to raise the airship near Baaj Temple.

The Tunnel Armor, otherwise known as TunnelArmr, is a boss in Final Fantasy VI. It is encountered by Locke and Celes on their way through the South Figaro Cave. The Twin Sentry is an enemy that appears in Chapter 10 of Dirge of Cerberus -Final Fantasy VII-. It is a stationary mounted heavy machine gun.

The Twin Stinger is a weapon for Cloud in Final Fantasy VII Remake. It provides the unique Counterstance ability, which causes Cloud to brace for an attack, then retaliate with a powerful slash dealing burst damage with an area-of-effect. Twin Stinger has balanced and attribute bonuses. Most importantly, the Twin Stinger is one of the only weapons to reach maximum materia capacity before Weapon Level 6. This gives Twin Stinger a wide variety of uses with various materia combinations. Overall, its unlocked abilities lend it slightly more towards casting spells, with its boost to Cloud's MP, as well as to both positive and negative status duration.

Ultima Buster, originally translated as Atma, is a boss in Final Fantasy VI. It is found in the final dungeon and is a stronger version of the Ultima Weapon. The boss appears in a prison cell room originally in Vector, standing in the spot Kefka stood in when he was arrested.

Tyranorox is a dragon/tyrant-type enemy in Final Fantasy XII found in the Crossover A area of the Henne Mines. It has a hammer as a rare drop. It can be defeated with Death and other instant death means as it does not have the Safety augment. Tyranorox also features as a boss on the Phon Coast in the Final Fantasy XII demo, only it is called Rockeater.

Ultima Weapon Majeure is an enemy that appears in Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis. Ultima Weapon Majeure appears as a boss in the "Weapon Showdown: Battle for the Planet" event and its associated Escalation Challenge. Players are also able to obtain a Memoria of Ultima Weapon Majeure during the event. Ultima Weapon Majeure was created by Sephiroth. Like its planetary counterpart, its purpose is to destroy all threats posed to the planet - but as Sephiroth's creation, it strengthens his control over the planet. The Lifestream has a multitude of possibilities flowing through it, and Sephiroth unleashed Ultima Weapon Majeure on all of them in a bid to erase them, absorbing the energy from the destroyed possibilities and further strengthening Sephiroth's control. Aerith Gainsborough, with help from Angeal Hewley, Zack Fair, Rosen, Glenn Lodbrok, Matt Winsord, and Lucia Lin, defeated multiple versions of Ultima Weapon Majeure. Aerith also summons Cloud Strife and his friends, who resonate with Aerith's will and band together to defeat the Weapon for good.

Weapon duplication is a famous glitch in the PlayStation version of Final Fantasy Tactics. It can only be done with one-handed weapons, and is commonly performed with the Excalibur and Save the Queen. It is done by switching a character to a class that can equip the weapon one wants copied, and giving him/her the Two Sword ability. The player must put a shield or weaker weapon in their top slot, and their weapon in the other, then select Best Fit. It should display the player's weapon in the top slot and the strongest available weapon in the bottom; if the weapon is not there, the glitch will not happen with that item. After pressing purchase, one should have a copy of the weapon duplicated. One can get up to 99 copies of any weapon the glitch works with, for nearly no gil.

The Wizard Staff bug is a bug in the original Famicom version of Final Fantasy II. When used as an item in battle, the Wizard's Staff (known as the Evil Staff in the Neo Demiforce fan translation and Wizard Staff in the Dark Shadow over Palakia prototype) casts Scourge XVI (translated as Aero/Bane respectively) on a random target. The spell targets a random targeting byte, which can cause it to hit enemies or party members. However, it can potentially target empty slots, typically slots which contained a defeated enemy, resulting in no effect. Amusingly, it may report that the Emperor was targeted by the spell; this is because the final boss battle against him uses a unique targeting byte which is not excluded from the spell's targeting.

Wrath of the Land is Red XIII's third and final limit break, which can be learned from his folio bear the end of the game, on weapon level 9. Unlike Red XIII's other limit breaks, it does not have a secondary effect (beyond being good at raising stagger) and only deals damage. It is based on his Earth Rave Limit from Final Fantasy VII. Wrath of the Land is Red XIII's strongest limit break. He begins to four fast claw swipes, followed by a twirl attack that hits three times, a spin attack that hits further four times, and finishing with a strong belly-flop. Wrath of the Land is strong and significantly raises the target's stagger if it did not outright kill them. As Wrath of the Land is a level 3 limit break, it can only be used after using other means to raise Red XIII's limit level, mostly synergy abilities with allies, meaning that the player will likely only see it in long battles, such as against lategame bosses.

The errand will take 8–9 days, costs 10,000 gil, and does not have a specific reward even if successful beyond the JP earned by the participants. The best-suited job for the errand is the ninja, and sending a chemist dramatically improves the chance of success, though errands will succeed if the player sends any three units for the maximum amount of days.

The Docklands Light Railway (DLR) is operated by high-floor, bi-directional, single-articulated cars with four doors on each side, with each train normally composed of two cars. The cars have no driver’s cab, although there is a small driver’s console concealed behind a locked panel at each car end from which the passenger service agent (PSA) can drive the car when necessary. Other consoles at each door opening allow the PSA to control door closure and make announcements whilst patrolling the train. Because of the absence of a driver’s position, the fully glazed car ends provide an excellent forward (or rear) view for passengers. Despite having high floors and being highly automated, the cars are derived from a German light-rail design intended for use in systems with elements of street running. All the cars that have operated on the system look similar, but there have been five separate types, of which three are still in operation on the DLR. A further car type, with quite different styling, was first displayed in March 2008 and is due to be in service before September 2008.

The Hunts Point Avenue station is an express station on the IRT Pelham Line of the New York City Subway, served by the 6 train at all times and the <6> train on weekdays in the peak direction. It is located at Hunts Point Avenue and Southern Boulevard in the Longwood neighborhood in the Bronx. This station opened in 1919 as part of the Interborough Rapid Transit Company (IRT)'s Pelham Line. The line was constructed as part of an agreement between New York City and two private transit operators to expand transit service across the city known as the Dual Contracts. The station exclusively served local trains until 1946, when rush-hour express service began. The Hunts Point Avenue station was renovated to become compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 in 2014.

The S – Rockaway Park Shuttle is a shuttle train service in on the New York City Subway. It connects with the train at Broad Channel station. This shuttle train provides service to the southern part of the Rockaway peninsula, with a terminus at Rockaway Park–Beach 116th Street. It operates on trackage that was part of the Long Island Rail Road until the mid-1950s. Beginning on February 1, 1962, the Rockaway Shuttle was lettered HH, and from November 26, 1967 to September 10, 1972, it was colored red and was extended to Euclid Avenue on the IND Fulton Street Line in between roughly midnight and 6:00 a.m., hours when the did not run to and from Far Rockaway. During the late night-early morning hours, the HH would operate from Euclid Avenue to Rockaway Park, then to Far Rockaway, and finally back to Euclid Avenue, thus earning this night owl service the unofficial nickname as Rockaway Round-Robin. Afterward, the designation CC (colored green) was used for the shuttle, although during rush hours this train was extended all the way to Bedford Park Boulevard on the IND Concourse Line in the . A streetcar, trolley, or trolley car (in North America) or tram, or tramcar (in Europe and Australia) is a railborne vehicle, lighter than a train, designed for the transport of passengers (and/or, very occasionally, freight) within, close to, or between villages, towns and/or cities. A streetcar differs from other forms of rail-based transport in that the tracks are partly or wholly laid in streets, which are shared to a greater or lesser extent with other road traffic.

The Subway-Surface Lines are five trolley car routes that are operated by the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority. They run along surface tracks in West Philadelphia and parts of Delaware County, Pennsylvania, and within a shared subway tunnel that runs eastward directly towards Center City Philadelphia. The eastern teminus for all five routes is 13th and Juniper Streets. The Subway-Surface Lines have been likened to trolley lines such as Boston's Green Line.

The River Line (stylized as River LINE) is a diesel tram-train light rail system in southern New Jersey, United States, that connects the cities of Camden and Trenton, New Jersey's capital. It is operated for New Jersey Transit by the Southern New Jersey Rail Group (SNJRG), which originally included Bechtel Group and Bombardier. Now that the project is in its operational phase, Bombardier is the only member of SNJRG.[1] The River Line is so named because the path between those two cities runs more or less parallel to the Delaware River.

The Tren Urbano (Urban Train) is a 10.7-mile (17.2 km) fully automated rapid transit system that serves the municipalities of San Juan, Guaynabo and Bayamón in Puerto Rico. Tren Urbano is currently made up of a single rapid transit route. It consists of 16 stations, ten of which are elevated, four at grade or in open cuttings, and two underground.

ARV's (Axiom Return Vehicles) were long-range spacecraft built by the BnL Corporation and tasked with delivering EVE units to Earth in order to scan for lifeforms. Probe ships used a laser scanning system in order to find firm, level ground on which to land. (The Axiom itself also uses the same laser scanning system to land on its docking station) The Axiom has two docking bays for ARV's (or Probe Ships). Once an EVE unit found an example of life, the ship was programmed to retrieve the unit and return it to the Axiom. WALL•E hitched a ride on one of these ships, as he had grown quite attached to this unit and couldn't resist being without it. The ship docked in the Axiom with the help of two docking robots. After that it was fueled by FIL-R fueler bot. The unloading of EVE units is handled by robotic arms, including 077 and 229.

Darrell Wallace Jr. (born October 8, 1993), also known as Bubba Wallace, is an American professional stock car racing driver. Previously, Wallace was signed as a development driver for Joe Gibbs Racing where Wallace competed in the NASCAR Camping World Truck Series, driving the No. 54 Toyota Tundra for Kyle Busch Motorsports. Afterwards, he raced in the Xfinity Series, driving the No. 6 Ford Mustang of Roush Fenway Racing, then he drove the no. 43 part time for Richard Petty Motorsports when Aric Almirola was injured in 2017, then was full time from 2018 to 2021.[1] He voiced Bubba Wheelhouse in Cars 3.
